reply.subject: RM_LadderPortable

observed.facings.png: Four facings at one shared scale. South: two small wooden caps side by side with carved tops, low in the frame. East: a short ladder lying on a diagonal, with two round stringers running left-right and rising toward the upper right, and five upright rungs between them with rope lashings and small iron end plates. North: a tall upright lashed wooden ladder, with two stringers whose carved tops stick up above the top rung, five flat rungs, X rope lashings, iron plates near the feet and a soft dark blurred edge around it. West: the east picture mirrored, rising toward the upper left.
observed.south.png: Two small rounded wooden stubs near the vertical centre of the canvas, about 27 px tall. Each shows a carved, fringed end-grain top over a short band, with a dark outline. No rung is visible between them. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: In the lower-right part of the canvas, a short ladder drawn on a diagonal. Its two cylindrical stringers have highlights and shadow and rise from lower left to upper right. Five round rungs run roughly up-down between them, each looking like a cylinder with thickness. There are rope lashings at the joints and small iron caps on the stringer ends. The outline is darker and heavier, and the surface smoother and more uniform brown, than the north art. Clean alpha, no cast shadow.
observed.north.png: The kept north art: a tall painterly lashed wooden ladder with wood grain, X rope bindings, riveted iron plates top and bottom, and carved stringer tops sticking up above the top rung. A soft dark blurred edge surrounds the silhouette.
observed.west.png: A mirror of east: the ladder in the lower-left of the canvas, stringers rising from lower right to upper left, rungs up-down, same lashings and iron caps.
observed.scale.png: All facings placed on a pit beside a vanilla pawn's head. North: the tall ladder stands on the north wall band with its tops above the rim. East: a short diagonal ladder crosses the right outline from the outside ground into the east wall band. West: its mirror on the left. South: two small nubs sit on the bottom outline. The east/west ladders are small next to the pawn's head.
observed.wall_context.png: Each facing composed on its wall. North wall: a tall ladder over the rim line on the light wall band. East wall: dark pit on the left, a light wall band, a black rim line, then ground. The ladder's upper-right end rests past the rim on the ground side, and it descends to the left across the band, with its lower-left foot at or very slightly past the band's inner edge into the dark. West wall: the mirror image, descending to the right. South wall: two small carved nubs sit right on the rim line, nothing else.
observed.variants_1.png: Vanilla reference strip (WallTorch, WallLamp, AncientEmergencyLight, LifesupportUnit, OxygenPump) in north/east/south. The south views show only a small cap or sliver at the top of the cell, and the east views a narrow profile.
observed.variants_2.png: Same image as wall_context.png: the four portable ladder facings on their walls.

CAMERA.seen: East/west show the stringers' tops lit, with the upper end higher on screen (height extends north). South shows end-grain caps seen from above at the rim. All facings use the building camera, not a side elevation.

BORE.seen: No pipe or hose. The stringer ends show carved wooden end grain, not an open bore.

PORTS.seen: No ports and no attached parts. No assembled capture is needed or given for a portless ladder.

WALL_LEAN.seen: In wall_context the east ladder rests its top at the east rim (right) and descends left into the pit. The west ladder mirrors it, top at the west rim, descending right. The lean matches each wall side.

WALL_AXIS.seen: East: the long axis runs east-west on screen (lower-left to upper-right diagonal), stringers left-right, rungs up-down. West: the mirror, also east-west. North: the long axis runs up/down the face. South: only nubs at the rim. None lies along its wall.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: The card lists no code ports, and no connector is drawn on any facing.

LAYERS.seen: No assembled multi-part view. The ladder is a single sprite.

ROTATIONS.seen: Same lashed wooden ladder with five rungs, rope bindings, iron end fittings and carved stringer tops on every facing. The east/west rendering is somewhat smoother, with a heavier outline than the painterly north, but it is the same object and palette family.

SIGNATURE.seen: It reads as a portable wooden ladder on every facing. The south nubs read as ladder tops poking over the near rim, like the vanilla reference south views.

MATERIAL.seen: Brown wood with shading and grain-like strokes, rope lashings and dark iron caps. It reads as wood, not paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Each facing sits where it should on its wall. East/west span from the rim across the wall band. The 737% height spread is a real pose difference (nubs vs a standing ladder vs a short side-wall ladder), not a size error.

ALPHA.seen: New facings have clean alpha with no backdrop or cast shadow. North (kept art) has a soft dark blurred edge, but north is an engine-limit keep.

OURS.seen: Project-specific lashed ladder matching the kept north. Not vanilla or another mod's art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: E/W now run east-west (up/down the wall), not north-south. They read as round 3D cylinders, not a flat squashed cutout. South is only two small nubs, not a truncated north. The E/W foot reaches the band's inner edge and at most touches the dark, so it does not run down into the pit.

LEGIBLE.seen: The east/west ladder fills only about 130x90 px of the 384 canvas, about 16x11 px at 32 px/cell, with rungs about 1 px wide. At normal zoom it likely reads as a small brown diagonal smudge. The south nubs are about 3 px tall at that zoom.

reply.subject: RM_LadderPortable
reply.image_seen: 1: four ladder facings on checkerboard; 2: two small wooden caps; 3: short horizontal ladder rising toward the right; 4: tall wooden ladder with lashings and metal plates; 5: mirrored horizontal ladder; 6: ladders around a pit beside a human; 7: the same pit composition; 8: enlarged individual wall compositions.

concerns.evidence: Images 3, 5 and 8 show smoother, more uniformly brown cylindrical stringers than the textured north ladder in image 4. This is a modest finish difference: side views still show rounded shading, wood markings, lashings and metal end plates, and remain recognizably the same ladder.

In images 6–8, the east ladder's lower left wooden end crosses the light wall band's inner boundary into the dark pit. The west ladder's lower right end does the mirrored equivalent. The projecting portion includes the outlined wooden end, rather than only an attached shadow.
Images 2–5 show solid wooden stringers and rungs with capped or plated ends. There is no pipe, hose or open bore whose plane could be wrong; the unconditional bore check is satisfied.
The card defines zero ports. Images 2–5 show wood, rope lashings and fastening plates, with no drawn hose, cord or coupler connector. The unconditional port check is satisfied.

Images 6–8 show plausible wall compositions, including south caps at the near rim, but no supplied image is identified as an assembled in-game capture. These compositions cannot verify the running game's altitude and wall occlusion order; captures of all four rotations are missing.
